learning.title: A reference check must not lock rows of an insert-only table
learning.trigger: A result-reference or existence check reads a table the application role can only select from and insert into, such as bakery.check_runs, and uses `for update` or `for key share`.
learning.mistake: assertCheckRunReference selected check_runs `for update of check_run`. PostgreSQL requires UPDATE privilege for every row lock, even FOR KEY SHARE, so the application role failed with permission denied the first time a result carried a real checkRunId. The earlier code never ran because no row could exist.
learning.rule: Read an insert-only table without a row lock. Nothing can change or delete the row before the transaction commits, so a lock adds no safety. Keep locks (`for key share`) only on tables the role may update, such as artifact_versions. Prove a new reference check with a real row through the application role, not the owner role.

verification.requirement: A completed quality.check result whose checkRunIds name rows written by the finalizer is accepted through the application role.

learning.boundary: Applies to tables with `grant select, insert` only; a table the role updates still needs the lock that protects against a concurrent change.
